findings.scenario: A --via-pool run against an existing invalid database path, or a database whose FTS extension/indexes cannot be queried, can report PLATEAU and exit successfully without exercising any FTS evict/reload workload.
findings.evidence: runViaPool logs initialization errors and continues collecting RSS samples; line 277 also converts every FTS query error to an empty result. Reproduced with $BREW_PREFIX/bin/node --expose-gc scripts/bench/fts-evict-reload-rss.mjs --via-pool package.json --cycles 6: all six opens failed with 'not a valid Lbug database file', yet the process exited 0, emitted MACHINE verdict PLATEAU, and claimed db.close() reclaims the FTS arena.
findings.recommendation: Track successful initialization and FTS queries per cycle. Abort on initialization failures and unexpected query errors; allow missing individual indexes only when at least one FTS query succeeds. Emit a failed or INCONCLUSIVE result when the workload was not exercised, rather than a memory-reclamation verdict.
